riskReasons: RHS accepts ‘Arakawa’ and records ‘Rough Bark Maple’ and ‘Rough Bark’ as synonyms, but those English labels can also be used descriptively in commerce.
Rough corky bark develops with age and is not reliable on young plants; bark texture alone cannot authenticate the cultivar.
Institutional size frameworks support a vigorous medium to larger tree and differ from compact nursery presentations.

duplicateCheck.notes: Compared with RC-003 ‘Sango-kaku’, CUL-000014 ‘Beni-kawa’, CUL-000018 ‘Aoyagi’ and other bark-interest maples. ‘Arakawa’ is distinct through its accepted name and age-dependent corky bark profile. ‘Arakawa-ukon’ is separately accepted; seedlings or ex-Arakawa material are not the cultivar. C0 resolves as unique.

identityNotes: The Atlas uses ‘Arakawa’ as the accepted working name. RHS-recorded English names are retained as aliases but should not be applied generically to every rough-barked Japanese maple. ‘Arakawa-ukon’ is a separate accepted cultivar, and material labelled ex ‘Arakawa’ does not preserve clonal identity.

content.summary: A vigorous upright Japanese maple valued for rough corky bark that develops after several years, with small green five-lobed leaves turning golden yellow and orange in autumn.
content.habit: Vigorous upright deciduous small to medium tree, forming a bushy crown and becoming a substantial garden specimen with age.
content.leafForm: Small palmate green leaves, described by RHS as finely dissected and five-lobed within the palmatum group. Foliage is secondary to the age-dependent bark character.

seasonal.spring: Green leaves emerge on smooth young growth; rough bark should not be expected on very young plants.
seasonal.summer: Foliage remains green while corky texture becomes more evident on older trunk and branches.
seasonal.autumn: Leaves turn golden yellow and orange; exact balance varies by season and site.

size.qualifier: RHS places the ultimate range at 4–8 m high and 2.5–4 m wide; JC Raulston lists 20–25 ft and measured one accession at 9 ft in 2015. Age and site materially affect both scale and bark development.

content.cultivation: Grow in moisture-retentive, well-drained soil in a sheltered position, in full sun to partial shade where moisture is reliable. Avoid excessive exposure and drought, which can cause leaf scorch.
content.diagnostic: Unlike coral- or green-stem cultivars, ‘Arakawa’ is defined by rough corky bark on older wood. Compare with ‘Arakawa-ukon’ and with seedlings sold as rough-bark maples; neither bark texture nor an English label alone proves clonal identity.
content.confidence: High confidence in accepted name, Acer palmatum placement, vigorous upright habit and age-dependent corky bark. Moderate confidence in alias scope, exact onset of bark expression and mature size.
content.unresolvedIssue: The English labels ‘Rough Bark Maple’ and ‘Rough Bark’ require context because they can function descriptively. The lean review does not establish a primary origin history or a universal age at which corking becomes conspicuous.
